title.es: Saltos atrás y adelante en el tiempo

es: Reconocer los saltos temporales de un relato (flashbacks y hechos anteriores) y los tiempos y marcadores que los señalan.

teaching.en: The film starts in Madrid, but a flashback takes us to Sara's childhood.
teaching.es: La película empieza en Madrid, pero un flashback nos lleva a la infancia de Sara.
teaching.explanationEs: Un flashback es un salto atrás; al volver a lo anterior, el relato cambia de tiempo verbal.
segments: The film starts in Madrid, but a
flashback takes us to Sara's childhood.
teaching.audioText: The film starts in Madrid, but a flashback takes us to Sara's childhood.

teaching.en: Sara was waiting at the gate; earlier, she had lost her passport.
teaching.es: Sara esperaba en la puerta de embarque; antes había perdido su pasaporte.
teaching.explanationEs: Had + participio marca un hecho anterior a otro del pasado; earlier lo refuerza.
segments: Sara was waiting at the gate;
earlier, she had lost her passport.
teaching.audioText: Sara was waiting at the gate; earlier, she had lost her passport.

teaching.en: She had been looking for it for an hour, and meanwhile the other passengers were boarding.
teaching.es: Llevaba una hora buscándolo y, mientras tanto, los demás pasajeros embarcaban.
teaching.explanationEs: Had been + -ing presenta una acción que venía durando; meanwhile y were + -ing marcan lo simultáneo.
segments: She had been looking for it for an
hour, and meanwhile the other passengers were boarding.
teaching.audioText: She had been looking for it for an hour, and meanwhile the other passengers were boarding.

teaching.en: Eventually, she found it in her coat, and she ran to the gate.
teaching.es: Por fin lo encontró en el abrigo y corrió a la puerta de embarque.
teaching.explanationEs: Eventually marca el final de la espera; el relato avanza en pasado simple.
segments: Eventually, she found it in her coat,
and she ran to the gate.
teaching.audioText: Eventually, she found it in her coat, and she ran to the gate.

teaching.en: Previously, she had never missed a flight.
teaching.es: Antes de eso, nunca había perdido un vuelo.
teaching.explanationEs: Previously + had + participio mira atrás desde un momento del pasado.
segments: Previously, she had never
missed a flight.
teaching.audioText: Previously, she had never missed a flight.

teaching.en: Afterwards, she laughed about it with her brother.
teaching.es: Después, se rio de ello con su hermano.
teaching.explanationEs: Afterwards marca lo que ocurre después, contado en pasado simple.
segments: Afterwards, she laughed about
it with her brother.
teaching.audioText: Afterwards, she laughed about it with her brother.

title.en: She was to become a legend

es: Formar was to, was to have + participio y would para contar destinos cumplidos y planes frustrados desde el pasado.

teaching.en: Her debut was a small concert, but she was to become a legend.

teaching.explanationEs: Was to + verbo base cuenta desde el pasado un destino que sí se cumplió.
segments: Her debut was a small concert, but
she was to become a legend.
teaching.audioText: Her debut was a small concert, but she was to become a legend.

teaching.en: Her career was to last forty years.

last forty years.

title.en: What was going on by then?

es: Extraer el orden y la duración de los hechos de una conversación sobre un viaje usando for, until, since, no sooner… than y hardly… when.

teaching.en: Our itinerary says we leave Lima at six and land in Madrid at noon.

six and land in Madrid at noon.

answer.text: My trip to Lima was terrible. My arrival was to have been on Monday at eight, but I missed my connection because the first flight had been delayed. To make things worse, the airline had lost my luggage, and I had been waiting for an hour when they finally found it. Meanwhile, I asked for a refund. The staff were kind, and they found me a room for the night. I told Mia that the plane left at nine, but that was a mistake: it left at ten, not nine. Now I am sitting at the airport, and I am very tired. By Wednesday, I will have arrived, and I will have been travelling for almost three days. This time next week, I will be lying on a beach, and I will have forgotten the delay.
accepted: My trip to Lima was terrible. My arrival was to have been on Monday at eight, but I missed my connection because the first flight had been delayed. To make things worse, the airline had lost my luggage, and I had been waiting for an hour when they finally found it. Meanwhile, I asked for a refund. The staff were kind, and they found me a room for the night. I told Mia that the plane left at nine, but that was a mistake: it left at ten, not nine. Now I am sitting at the airport, and I am very tired. By Wednesday, I will have arrived, and I will have been travelling for almost three days. This time next week, I will be lying on a beach, and I will have forgotten the delay.

Let me tell you about my trip to Lima. My arrival was to have been on Monday, but the first flight had been delayed, so I missed my connection. When I finally reached the airport, the airline had already lost my luggage, and I had been waiting for an hour before they found it. I asked for a refund, and the staff were kind enough to find me a room for the night. I wrote to Mia that the plane left at nine. Sorry, that was a mistake: it left at ten, not nine. At the moment I am waiting for a new flight, and I am very tired. By Wednesday, I will have arrived, and I will have been travelling for three days. This time next week, I will be sitting on a beach, and I will have forgotten the whole delay.

feedback.es: La cronología necesita had + participio para lo anterior, was to have been para el plan frustrado, will have / will be para el futuro y una corrección con not.

origin.text: Caso: tu vuelo a Lima tenía que llegar el lunes a las ocho. El primer vuelo se había retrasado, perdiste la conexión y la aerolínea había perdido tu equipaje; estuviste una hora esperando. Pediste un reembolso. Le contaste a Mia que el vuelo salió a las nueve, pero fue un error: salió a las diez. Cuenta qué había pasado antes, qué plan no se cumplió, cuándo habrás llegado (el miércoles, tras casi tres días de viaje) y qué estarás haciendo dentro de una semana (en la playa).
